what_its_for: Deferasirox is used to remove excess iron from your body. This buildup of iron can happen when you receive many blood transfusions (for conditions like sickle cell disease or thalassemia) or when your body absorbs too much iron on its own. Too much iron in your body can damage your heart, liver, and other organs, so this medicine helps get rid of the extra iron through your urine and stool.
how_to_take: How you take deferasirox depends on which form you have. EXJADE (dispersible tablets): Do NOT swallow whole. Drop the tablet(s) into a glass of water, orange juice, or apple juice and stir until fully dissolved into a fine liquid. Drink it right away. Rinse the glass with a little more liquid and drink that too so you get the full dose. Take it on an EMPTY stomach, at least 30 minutes before eating. JADENU (film-coated tablets): Swallow whole with water or other liquids. Take it on an EMPTY stomach OR with a light snack (less than 7% fat, such as yogurt or an apple). JADENU SPRINKLE (granules): Sprinkle the granules onto soft foods like yogurt or applesauce. Eat right away — do not store for later. Take with a light meal or snack. Take deferasirox ONCE DAILY at the same time each day. Do not crush or chew the film-coated Jadenu tablets.
dosing: Your doctor will calculate your dose based on your body weight (in kilograms) and the reason you are taking it. Typical starting doses range from 7 mg/kg/day to 20 mg/kg/day. Your doctor will adjust your dose over time based on your iron levels (measured by a blood test called serum ferritin) and how well you tolerate the medicine. Never change your dose on your own. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribes.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember ON THAT SAME DAY. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next regular dose at the usual time. Do NOT take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the medicine in its original container or packaging, tightly closed. Protect from moisture and heat — do NOT store in a bathroom medicine cabinet. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids that contain aluminum (such as Maalox or Mylanta) while taking deferasirox, as they can interfere with how the medicine works. Avoid taking other iron-chelating (iron-removing) medicines at the same time unless your doctor specifically tells you to. Avoid drinking grapefruit juice, as it can affect the level of medicine in your blood. Avoid using anti-inflammatory pain relievers (NSAIDs) like ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) or naproxen (Aleve) unless approved by your doctor, as combining them can increase the risk of kidney problems or stomach bleeding. Avoid drinking alcohol excessively, as it may worsen liver effects. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting deferasirox.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: dark, tarry, or bloody stools or vomit that looks like coffee grounds (signs of stomach or intestinal bleeding); sudden decrease in the amount of urine you make, swelling in your legs or feet, or foamy urine (signs of kidney problems); yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain (signs of liver problems); severe skin rash, blistering, or peeling; sudden loss of vision or hearing; high fever, confusion, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if you have: persistent nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, or diarrhea; unusual tiredness or weakness; dizziness or fainting. Regular blood tests to check your kidneys, liver, and iron levels are very important — do not skip your follow-up appointments.
when_it_works: Deferasirox starts working right away to bind iron in your body, but it takes weeks to months before you will see a meaningful drop in your iron levels (ferritin levels in your blood). Your doctor will check your ferritin levels every month to monitor progress. Most patients begin to see noticeable improvement in iron levels after several months of consistent daily use. Continue taking this medicine every day even if you feel fine — iron overload usually has no symptoms until it causes serious organ damage.
special_populations: Children: Deferasirox can be used in children as young as 2 years old. Jadenu Sprinkle granules are especially helpful for young children who cannot swallow tablets. The dose is based on body weight. Children need regular monitoring of growth, kidney function, and liver function. Elderly (65 and older): Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, especially kidney problems. Doctors should monitor kidney function closely and may start at a lower dose. Pregnancy: It is not known if deferasirox is safe during pregnancy. Tell your doctor immediately if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or become pregnant while taking this medicine. Breastfeeding: It is not known if deferasirox passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Kidney or liver problems: If you already have kidney or liver disease, deferasirox may not be safe for you or may require a lower dose or more frequent monitoring. Your doctor will decide if this medicine is appropriate for you.
